audio_caption: The audio begins with a male speaker introducing an instructional video on formatting a paper in APA style using Microsoft Word on a Macintosh operating system, noting that it will cover style rules for the sixth edition. The speaker then goes on to describe basic Mac operating system features like window positioning and resizing, mentioning how to zoom in or out to adjust text size.

The clip begins with a single male speaker describing an interface resembling Word 2007 and 2010 on Windows, highlighting the "ribbon at the top of the window" and the organization of "menu options by category." He mentions that "most familiar menu options can be found in the home tab" but notes that "all menu options are also available in the bar at the top of the screen, where menus for all applications appear."

An individual is heard giving instructions, characterized by a calm and instructive tone, related to "formatting your template for APA style". They guide the listener to "click on file... and click on page setup", then to "choose Microsoft Word for settings". Further instructions include to "set all four margins to one inch", and to be aware that "your header and footer should be one half inch from the edges", and finally to "click on layout options".

The audio clip begins with a single male voice discussing APA style, mentioning the requirement for a different header format on the first page and how to set this preference. He then explains how to save time by making this the default setting for future templates. This voice suddenly stops abruptly.

The audio begins with one male speaker explaining how to adjust margins by hovering over the edge until two arrows appear. The speaker also notes the independence of text from margins and the control one has over text placement via arrows. Then, the speaker advises going to the top menu bar, clicking "format," and "font" for precise text settings.

The audio begins with a male speaker explaining that APA style requires the use of Times New Roman 12-point font throughout the manuscript, except for figures, where a sans-serif font is preferred. He gives instructions to "choose the correct font and size", then he suggests to click ok or to choose default to maintain the same setting on future documents. Next, the speaker continues by instructing the listener to click format in the same menu and choose the "paragraph" option. Finally there is a sound, which it's hard to identify.

The clip features one male speaker, giving instructions. He uses a normal tone while he requests specific formatting for a manuscript, including indentation, double spacing, and the removal of extra spaces.

The audio begins with a male speaker discussing formatting options, cautioning against using "widow orphan control" due to its potential for creating unnecessary space. His tone is instructional. Next, the same speaker shifts to explaining how to insert a header, directing the listener to "view" in the top menu bar. The audio ends abruptly before the complete instruction is provided.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker pointing out a new tab in the ribbon. He describes moving between the header and text, then references a header footer tab and page numbers. The speaker then speaks the word "Alright".

The clip starts with a male speaker giving instructions, including the phrases "running head" and "tab key," in a clear and informative tone. This transitions into the sound of typing, suggesting someone is following the speaker's instructions. Then the typing stops.

The audio begins with instructions on how to type in a main document, suggesting to "double click in the body of the text," "click enter a couple of times," and to then "begin typing the title." The speaker describes how to capitalize the title and subtitle, and mentions that "APA style includes all major words" to be a certain part of speech, including conjunctions and prepositions. The speaker further describes to add one's name below the title, and then the university or institution. The clip concludes with a single "pop" sound.

A male speaker starts by giving instructions to use the top menu and select certain options. He then suggests an alternative to pressing enter many times, promising more accurate page formatting. Afterward, he instructs to put the word abstract on the second page. Then, the speaker provides further instructions to insert another page break. Next, the speaker instructs to type the title or copy it from the first page. The speaker instructs again, directing the listener to set the text flush left with the first line indentation. The man wraps up by saying that the abstract is the only paragraph in the manuscript that is not indented.

The clip begins with one male speaker giving instructions on how to insert a header onto additional pages. He says to "double click in the header position," and to "copy the header and page number." His tone is informative. He continues to instruct, noting, "the page numbers will be automatic." He tells the listener to "make sure the typeface remains Times New Roman."

The audio clip starts with a male speaker giving instructions about formatting text, including creating a page break and removing indentation. He then instructs the listener to center the word "references" at the top of the page and discusses setting hanging indentation using either the ruler or the format paragraph option. The speaker suggests consulting an APA manual for proper reference formatting. At the end of the clip, the speaker says "Yeah."

The audio clip begins with a male speaker explaining that APA requires the use of an en-dash when noting a range of numbers. He then explains how to insert an en-dash using the top menu bar, by selecting "symbol," then "advanced symbol." He indicates how to select the en-dash and set up a keyboard shortcut, which he also explains. The audio clip ends with a woman's voice, uttering a single word.

The clip starts with a single male voice, explaining the size difference between a hyphen, en dash, and em dash, emphasizing their specific purposes in APA style. He then describes how to manually create an en dash, mentioning typing page numbers with spaces and a hyphen, which will transform into an en dash when followed by a period or space, requiring subsequent removal of the added spaces. Subsequently, a popping sound is heard.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker providing instructions. He suggests finding instructional videos online or googling questions, emphasizing that hands-on experience is the best way to learn a program. Continuing, he mentions the APA style PowerPoint on the Kennesaw State Psychology Lab webpage and the APA publication manual, ending with "Thank you for watching."
